title: File:Striga hermonthica flowering among maize and cassava in Uganda.jpg
description:
Flowering plant of _Striga hermonthica_, commonly called purple witchweed, growing in an agricultural field in Uganda. The image shows clusters of small tubular purple-pink flowers with five lobes, growing among maize and cassava.
_Striga hermonthica_ is a hemiparasitic herb native to sub-Saharan Africa. It attaches to the roots of cereal crops like maize and sorghum to extract water and nutrients, which gives it the common name "witchweed". The plant occurs naturally in farmlands and grasslands across Uganda during the rainy season. This photograph documents the species in its natural agricultural habitat, showing both its floral structure and ecological context.
